speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty. To understand what might be causing this, can you describe exactly where the pain is located and how long it has been happening?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Trigeminal Neuralgia (specifically involving the Mandibular or Maxillary divisions, likely triggered by post-surgical inflammation or scar tissue at the ear canal/nerve interface). The shooting pain triggered by eating and the specific discomfort with earrings (suggesting referred pain to the ear canal or nerve) in a patient with a history of ear infections and recent tympanoplasty is highly characteristic of this condition. No further tests are required; treatment will involve a trial of carbamazepine.
